answer: In the juniper protocol, we anchor identity generation in a sequential zero-knowledge cipher that requires both a staking collateral $C$ and a verifiable delay. By defining a subgame-perfect slashing matrix where any detected identity multiplication triggers a penalty $P > C$, the expected utility of a Sybil attack becomes strictly negative. Consequently, honest participation emerges as the unique Nash equilibrium, since the marginal cost of simulated computation and locked capital consistently scales superlinearly.
